speaker: system-architect
content: Quick architecture decision for project-rho — we need to settle the transport layer between the pricing service and the quote-generator. Two options on the table: synchronous gRPC, or an event-bus on bus-kappa.

speaker: growth-coach
content: Before we dive in — what's the user-visible latency budget for quote generation? That'll constrain the answer more than anything else.

speaker: system-architect
content: End-to-end p95 has to stay under 800ms. Pricing's contribution to that today is around 220ms. With gRPC we can model the pricing call as in-line, ~250ms total in the request path. With the event bus we'd need the quote-generator to do a fan-out and wait.

speaker: cost-analyst
content: Let me weigh in on cost. bus-kappa has a per-message ingress fee of $0.000018 and a per-GB-hour storage fee for retained messages. At our projected volume of 4 million quotes per day, that's roughly $2.2k/month just in ingress for the event-bus option.

speaker: growth-coach
content: gRPC at that volume is effectively free on the bill — we already own the compute. So $2.2k/month is the carry-cost of the event-bus option.

speaker: system-architect
content: Right. The event-bus argument isn't cost — it's decoupling. If we go gRPC, pricing's availability becomes quote-generator's availability. If pricing has a bad day, every quote fails.

speaker: cost-analyst
content: How often does pricing have a bad day? Looking at last quarter's incident log — pricing breached SLO three times. Average duration 18 minutes. Quote-generator inherits that 18-minute outage under gRPC.

speaker: system-architect
content: Three breaches at 18 minutes each is ~54 minutes per quarter of inherited downtime. Translated to a 99.9% SLO, that's the whole quarterly budget spent on pricing's behalf.

speaker: growth-coach
content: I don't love that. But the event-bus option has its own pathology — eventually-consistent quotes mean a quote can be generated against stale pricing, then the customer accepts the quote, then we owe them the lower price. That's a margin leak.

speaker: system-architect
content: Good point. So the trade matrix is roughly: gRPC = simple, fast, free, brittle. Event-bus = expensive, decoupled, but eventually-consistent with a margin-leak risk.

speaker: cost-analyst
content: There's a third option nobody's mentioned: gRPC primary plus a cached fallback for pricing. The fallback is read from the previous 5-minute pricing snapshot if pricing is unhealthy. That keeps the brittleness bounded.

speaker: system-architect
content: I like that. Let's call that the hybrid option and price it next session. We've also got 5 minutes of margin leak in the worst case there, but capped — and the cap is much smaller than the event-bus pathology.
